title: Redwood February 2026 All-Hands
summary: Monthly company all-hands covering Q4 results, product roadmap highlights (Dedicated, Private, Optimize), ops updates, hiring and hiring freeze lift, and an open Q&A. Leadership recapped priorities: reliability, cost optimization, and private deployments. Action items include follow-ups on security docs, sales enablement materials, and a cross-team benchmark for latency improvements.
next_steps: Share slide deck and recorded video (links in #all-hands)
SE team to run cross-team latency benchmark (due 2026-02-23)
Product to publish Dedicated capacity playbook by 2026-02-18
Security to circulate SOC2 roadmap and compliance FAQ
action_items: Samir Desai: run end-to-end latency benchmark for typical customer workloads (due 2026-02-23)
Liam O'Connor: publish Dedicated capacity playbook + rollout checklist (due 2026-02-18)
Zoe Kim: update hiring plan and post new IC roles (due 2026-02-16)
Jordan Lee: provide updated revenue and runway slides for Board packet (due 2026-02-12)
Security Team: share SOC 2 timeline and answers to top 10 security questions (due 2026-02-20)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-09 10:00 PST — Duration: 60 minutes — Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Priya, Liam, Zoe, Jordan, Ava, Samir and all staff

[00:00] Maya Patel: Good morning, everyone, thanks for joining—um, happy February. Quick housekeeping, recording's on uh video and transcript will be posted in #all-hands. We'll run through highlights and then leave plenty of time for Q&A.

[00:35] Carlos Rivera: Quick note on infra, we've seen steady improvement in 99th percentile latency after the kernel selection updates. There's still some tail at high concurrency, we're working on better batching heuristics.

[01:10] Priya Singh: The continuous batching work reduced token cost by roughly 12% in our internal tests; caveat that numbers vary by prompt distribution. Samir is running a broader benchmark to validate across customer workloads.

[01:45] Samir Desai: yeah, the benchmark plan is to sweep models, sequence lengths, and quantization profiles — we want to capture both latency and cost per 1k tokens so we can provide concrete guidance. I'll own the run and share results.

[02:20] Liam O'Connor: On product, Dedicated got a few new autoscaling features: burst capacity and per-pool retention policies. We're also shipping a Dedicated playbook that walks customers through capacity sizing and rollout. Link to draft: https://redwood.internal/dedicated-playbook (posted in #product).

[03:05] Ava Martinez: On go-to-market, we've started a vertical push into fintech; the playbook will be critical for sales to size deals. Also note a few inbound POC requests mention VPC-only deployments as a must.

[03:40] Jordan Lee: Financials — Q4 outperformed plan, ARR growth at 42% YoY, runway extended by the Series C collar; we'll include updated slides in the board packet. Quick ask: product and sales, please freeze any non-essential spends for next two weeks while we finalize bookings.

[04:15] Zoe Kim: Hiring update — we've lifted the hiring freeze for product and infra IC roles; we'll prioritize senior infra and SE hires. Please expect outreach for referrals.

[04:50] Maya Patel: Thanks Zoe. On company priorities this quarter: 1) Reliability (SLOs and graceful degradation), 2) Cost/performance tooling (Optimize), and 3) Private deployments (VPC / on-prem readiness). We'll measure success by latency SLO attainment, cost per 1k tokens improvements, and two customer private deployments by end of Q2.

[05:30] Carlos Rivera: On reliability, we plan an SLO sprint next week to harden fallback policies and cross-region routing behavior. Note: KV cache work had a small regression in a canary — it was a config mismatch (someone read it as K-V cash in the notes, lol) — fix is in PR.

[06:05] Priya Singh: Also rolling out improved tracing hooks so ops can link slow requests to model versions and infra nodes. This should shorten MTTR for model-serving incidents.

[06:40] Employee 1 (Slack Q): any update on Private deployment pricing and contract terms?

[06:55] Liam O'Connor: We're finalizing a new Private pricing band for regulated customers — aim is to have standard terms by Feb 18. For on-prem, we'll require an installation window and support SLA. We'll circulate the draft.

[07:30] Employee 2: what's the plan for open-source models and Redwood-verified profiles?

[07:45] Carlos Rivera: We continue to curate a model catalog; verification means we publish latency/cost profiles and quality baselines. We're adding more quantized variants so customers can pick the right tradeoff. There will be a public doc and an internal toolkit for model onboarding.

[08:20] Maya Patel: Quick note on security — SOC 2 is in progress, controls mapping is 70% done, we expect a readiness assessment by mid-March. Security will share a FAQ and the timeline by end of next week.

[08:55] Jordan Lee: Also, for sales and finance, please use the new quota tool for forecasting — it'll be mandatory for next board deck.

[09:20] Q&A sequence — several folks asked about parental leave policy, which Zoe answered: updates to policy are being drafted and will be published to HR. There was a clarifying question about SSO/SAML and RBAC for Private customers, Security will cover in the FAQ.

[11:00] Employee 3: can we get more visibility into individual team OKRs?

[11:15] Maya Patel: Yes, starting next month we'll have a short 'team spotlight' in each all-hands where two teams present the top 3 OKRs and progress.

[11:45] Priya Singh: Technical deep-dive: our compiler/kernels work is enabling a 1.3x throughput increase on longer sequences for certain models. We're also evaluating AVX-512 paths on some clouds. We'll run a technical brown bag next week for folks interested.

[12:30] Carlos Rivera: Note — there was a customer POC where latency spiked at scale due to a mis-configured autoscaler; ops playbook now includes an autoscaler checklist. We linked the post-mortem in #ops.

[13:05] Maya Patel: Alright, wrapping up — big thanks to everyone, especially infra and SE for the benchmarks and the on-call rotations. Remember to review the playbook drafts and contribute feedback.

[13:35] Closing: links: slides + recording posted in #all-hands, Dedicated playbook draft: https://redwood.internal/dedicated-playbook, SOC2 timeline doc: https://redwood.internal/security/soc2. Action items and next steps will be posted.

End of transcript.
